chunks: What Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who recites one single surah in the two rakʿahs of the obligatory prayer while he is able to recite other than it. If he does that, what is upon him? He said: If he is able to recite other than it, then he should not do so; but if he is not able to recite other than it, then there is no harm.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs of the prayer under discussion
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or blame
key_terms.يُحْسِنُ: is able to recite well or properly

ai.seo_question: Can the same surah be recited in both rakʿahs of an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding reciting the same surah in both rakʿahs of an obligatory prayer. If a person can properly recite other surahs, he should not restrict himself to one surah in both rakʿahs; however, if he cannot recite other than that surah, then there is no problem.
